name: Metallic Paint
description: WebGL2 shader that turns a logo image or text into a liquid chrome shape with flowing metallic stripes, color dispersion, and a mouse-driven tilt, with an optional pour-in intro.
contents: Container div with a single WebGL2 canvas filling it
Shape taken from an image (SVG or raster) or from a text string
behavior: Chrome stripes flow continuously across the shape and distort with noise
Pointer movement over the container tilts the reflection with spring physics, and it eases back on leave
Pour-in reveal intro runs on first render when intro is true
Animation pauses when offscreen, when paused is true, or when the user prefers reduced motion
Canvas resizes with the container and redraws when props change
editableByProps: Shape source through imageSrc or text, with fontFamily and fontWeight for text
Stripe density, softness, dispersion, distortion, edge bend and angle
Animation speed, pause, intro reveal, mouse tilt strength
Shape scale and rotation, light or dark chrome mode
Pixel ratio and container sizing through className and style

needsCodeEdit.change: Change the base chrome colors of the stripes
needsCodeEdit.where: color1 and color2 lines in the FRAGMENT shader main function
The 1600 value in the reveal progress calculation inside the frame function
stiffness and damping constants in the frame function

fixed: Nothing renders without imageSrc or text, the canvas stays empty
Requires WebGL2, renders nothing if unavailable
Root is relative h-full w-full, so the parent must have a defined height or it collapses
Images that are fully opaque are converted to a shape by treating light pixels as transparent, so use dark logos on a light or transparent background
Remote images need CORS headers because they are read into a texture
Minimum render pixel ratio is 2 and total pixels are capped by MAX_PIXELS
Pointer tilt uses pointer events only on the container, with no touch-specific alternative beyond touch pointer movement
Respects prefers-reduced-motion by disabling motion and the intro
